summary.text: Alessandra Soliven is Labor's candidate for Pakenham at the 2026 Victorian election, standing for a seat whose sitting Labor MP is retiring. She is an organiser with the Australian Services Union, previously worked for an MP as an electorate officer, and is a law student at the University of Melbourne. Her party says she moved to Australia from the Philippines with her family and is the daughter of a nurse.

priorities.text: Health care that local families can get to easily, with more nurses
Better schools in the Pakenham area
More secure jobs so working families can get ahead

sources.title: Pakenham: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Alessandra Soliven, Candidate for Pakenham, Victorian Labor

summary.text: Kate Hands is the Libertarian candidate for Pakenham at the 2026 Victorian election. She has lived in the Pakenham and Cardinia area for more than two decades, has run small businesses, and has also had jobs in health care, social services and local government. She says she never planned a political career, and lists local involvement with junior sport, Neighbourhood Watch and the Yakerboo festival.

priorities.text: I want to see government get back to doing the basics well
Less government waste and lighter pressure on households and businesses
Smaller government, lower taxes and individual rights
Sensible laws on crime
No spin, no games, no corruption.

sources.title: Pakenham: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News
Kate Hands, Pakenham, Election 2026, Libertarians Victoria

summary.text: Nasser Yawari is the Greens candidate for Pakenham at the 2026 Victorian election. He came to Australia as a refugee, holds a sociology degree, and works at Victoria Legal Aid as a non-legal practitioner as well as with Jesuit Social Services. He was sixth on the Greens' Victorian Senate ticket at the 2025 federal election.

priorities.text: Easing the rising cost of living in Pakenham
Ending the major parties' reliance on donations from billionaires and large companies
Giving marginalised and multicultural communities a say in the decisions that affect them
Help for people facing unemployment, homelessness and poor access to services, which he says he has seen in his work

sources.title: Pakenham: 2026 Victorian election guide, ABC News

summary.text: Radmila Dyson is the Liberal candidate for Pakenham at the 2026 Victorian election. A businesswoman, she co-founded the Officer soccer club and founded table tennis and badminton clubs in Officer. The ABC reports that she had been a party member for under a year when she was preselected and needed special approval to stand.

summary.text: Raymond French is an independent candidate for Pakenham at the 2026 Victorian election. He works in pest control as director of The Harry's Group, a business that inspects and treats properties for buyers and developers. He was formerly a director of the Master Builders Association of Victoria and chaired its committee for the housing subcontracting sector.

prior_roles.role: Director and chairperson, housing subcontracting sector committee

summary.text: Stephanie Davies is an independent candidate for Pakenham at the 2026 Victorian election, on the VEC's list of nominations. She won Toomuc Ward on Cardinia Shire Council in 2020 and narrowly lost it in 2024, when she was listed as Stephanie Marie Davies. She contested the council's choice of a name for the new suburb in Pakenham East, raising it as a councillor in 2024 and later taking it to the Supreme Court of Victoria.

previous_candidacies.note: The VEC's council results carry no party labels; recorded as independent, as in 2024.

summary.text: Stephanie Grigg is the Victorian Socialists candidate for Pakenham at the 2026 Victorian election. A graphic designer and activist from the area, she has helped organise opposition to the state government's plans for public housing through the Public Housing Defence Network. Someone of the same name stood for the Victorian Socialists in Cardinia Shire's Henty Ward in 2024; the sources don't say whether it was her.

previous_candidacies.note: Wikipedia's 2024 results list a Stephanie Grigg for the Victorian Socialists in Henty Ward; no source confirms she is the 2026 candidate.

priorities.text: we can radically transform society to put people before profit
Immediate cost of living relief such as rent freezes, cheaper groceries and free lunches at school
A government-owned builder to add public housing, and undoing the privatisation of public services
Much more money for schools and hospitals
Keeping only an average worker's wage if elected and giving the rest to community programs

summary.text: Warren Pickering is the One Nation candidate for Pakenham at the 2026 Victorian election, and has been leader of the party's Victorian branch since August 2026. Born in Gippsland, he did farm work and bricklaying before about ten years as an Army combat engineer, with deployments to the Middle East, and later worked in coal mining in Queensland. He was One Nation's lead upper house candidate in Eastern Victoria in 2022 and headed its Victorian Senate ticket in 2022 and 2025, without winning a seat.

occupation.text: Former Army combat engineer; has also worked as a bricklayer and in coal mining

legal_and_integrity.text: Lost his driver's licence three times for drink driving, which he acknowledged publicly in September 2026; the ABC dates his drink driving to his twenties.
legal_and_integrity.note: Known only from his own admission as reported by Wikipedia (citing The Age) and the ABC; the sources give no dates and don't say whether a court or police imposed each loss of licence.
